fields.name: North
fields.tagline: Lively towns, beaches and cultural spots.
fields.description: Charming towns, historic landmarks and golden beaches: discover the vibrant spirit of the North
fields.about_text: The North is a captivating blend of heritage, culture and natural beauty. From lush gardens and historic landmarks to vibrant towns and dreamy beaches, the North offers something special for every traveler.
fields.travel_tip: Visit the beaches and Grand Baie early in the morning or late afternoon to avoid the midday heat and crowds, and enjoy the best light for sunsets.

fields.name: South
fields.tagline: Wild landscapes, heritage sites and scenic beauty.
fields.description: Discover the wild and untouched beauty of southern Mauritius, where dramatic coastline cliffs meet lush green valleys waiting to be explored. From towering waterfalls to hidden beaches, every turn offers a breathtaking new adventure just waiting for you.
fields.about_text:
The south is a land of contrasts and deep history. It carries the legacy of resilience and the struggle for freedom, reflected in places like Le Morne Brabant, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
From spiritual sites and natural wonders to authentic local experiences, the South offers a journey like no other.
fields.travel_tip: The best time to visit the South is from May to December for pleasant weather and calm seas. Don't forget to respect nature and local heritage sites during your visit.

fields.name: East
fields.tagline: Where the ocean meets authentic charm
fields.description: The East of Mauritius is a paradise of turquoise lagoons, powdery beaches, lush greenery and vibrant culture — offering the perfect escape for relaxation, adventure and unforgettable memories.
fields.about_text: The East is a blend of natural beauty, cultural heritage and tranquil villages. From idyllic islands and waterfalls to historic temples and lush landscapes, it offers a slower pace of life and authentic Mauritian experiences.
fields.travel_tip:
The best time to explore the East is from May to December for pleasant weather and calm seas.

Don't forget your sunscreen, light clothing and a camera to capture the stunning scenery and memories!

fields.name: West
fields.tagline: Sunset views, beaches and adventure experiences.
fields.description: From stunning beaches and turquoise waters to lush mountains and cultural treasures, the West invites you to relax, explore and create unforgettable memories.
fields.about_text: The West is one of Mauritius' most beloved regions, known for its long sandy beaches, crystal-clear lagoons, and spectacular sunsets. It is also home to lush nature reserves, charming villages, historical landmarks, and a wide range of activities for every type of traveller.
fields.travel_tip: The best time to explore the West is from May to December for pleasant weather, calm seas and unforgettable sunsets. Don't forget your sunscreen, hat and camera to capture every beautiful moment!
fields.keywords: west tamarin flic en flac sunset

fields.name: Central
fields.tagline: Green heart of the island, rivers, parks and local life.
fields.description: From dormant volcanoes and rolling hills to historical mansions and cascading waterfalls - explore the authentic heart of the Central Mauritius.
fields.about_text:
The Central Region is the cultural and geographic
 part of Mauritius. It is home to volcanic craters, lush forests,
 historic buildings and lively towns. 
From breathtaking viewpoints to serene  natural spots, 
the Central offers a perfect mix of heritage, 
adventure and relaxation.
fields.travel_tip:
The best time to explore the Central is from May to December for cooler weather and clear skies.

Wear comfortable shoes for hikes, carry water and don't forget your camera for unforgettable views!
fields.list_title: Discover the Best of the Central

fields.name: Aapravasi Ghat
fields.description: UNESCO World Heritage site marking the arrival point of indentured labourers to Mauritius in 1834.

fields.name: Le Morne Brabant Heritage Walk
fields.description: Guided walk telling the story of Le Morne as a refuge for escaped slaves — a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

fields.name: Fort Adelaide (Citadel)
fields.description: A 19th-century British fort overlooking Port Louis, with panoramic harbour views.

fields.name: National History Museum
fields.description: Housed in an 18th-century colonial mansion, exhibits cover naval battles, colonial life and Dutch/French/British rule.

fields.name: Blue Penny Museum
fields.description: Home to the famous 'Blue Penny' and 'Orange Penny' stamps and colonial-era maritime artifacts.

fields.name: St Louis Cathedral
fields.description: Located in the capital of Port Louis, St. Louis Cathedral is one of the oldest Catholic churches in Mauritius, originally built in the 18th century during French colonial rule. Its iconic stone facade and twin towers stand as a historic landmark and a central seat for the Roman Catholic Diocese of Port-Louis.

fields.name: Marie Reine de La Paix
fields.description: Perched on the slopes of Signal Mountain, Marie Reine de la Paix is an open-air Catholic shrine featuring a prominent 3-meter statue of the Virgin Mary unveiled during World War II in 1940. Visitors climb 82 steps across terraced gardens to reach the monument, which offers panoramic views of Port Louis and serves as a major site for pilgrimages and papal visits.

fields.name: Jummah Mosque
fields.description: Located in the heart of Port Louis, the Jummah Mosque. It stands as the main mosque in Mauritius and a serene sanctuary known for its ornate white facade, carved wooden doors, and historic courtyard.

fields.name: Chateau de Labourdonnais
fields.description: Built between 1856 and 1859 by Christian Wiehe, the Château de Labourdonnais is a grand neoclassical plantation house nestled in Mapou, surrounded by lush orchards and sugarcane fields. Now a beautifully restored museum, it offers a glimpse into 19th-century colonial island life, complete with period decor, fruit orchards, and an artisanal rum distillery.

fields.name: Kwan Tee Pagoda
fields.description: Inaugurated in 1842 by Hahime Choissane, the Kwan Tee Pagoda in Les Salines, Port Louis, is the oldest Chinese temple in Mauritius and the Southern Hemisphere. Dedicated to Guan Di, the god of righteousness and protection, its traditional red-and-gold architecture remains a central spiritual sanctuary and symbol of heritage for the Sino-Mauritian community.

fields.name: Grand Bassin
fields.description: Nestled in a secluded crater lake in the central highlands, Grand Bassin (Ganga Talao) is a sacred Hindu site in Mauritius. The natural lake is surrounded by colorful temples drawing hundreds of thousands of pilgrims during the annual Maha Shivaratri festival.

fields.name: Traditional Craft Workshop
fields.description: Discover Mauritian craftsmanship in a hands-on workshop. Learn about traditional materials and techniques while creating a piece to take home.

fields.name: Spend Time with a Mauritian Family
fields.description: Share a relaxed visit with a local Mauritian family. Enjoy conversation, learn about everyday island life and spend time over a friendly game of dominoes.

fields.name: Sega Experience
fields.description: Feel the rhythm of Mauritius with a lively sega performance. Discover the music, movement and cultural traditions behind this much-loved island dance.

fields.name: Join a Local Cuisine Experience
fields.description: Get close to the flavours of Mauritius in a local cooking experience. Watch a dish come together, discover familiar island ingredients and enjoy the aromas of the kitchen.

fields.name: Go Fishing
fields.description: Head out onto the lagoon with local fishers and experience a traditional day on the water, surrounded by the clear blue sea of Grand Baie.
